G2590.n: In Gal 5:22 it is singular, while the works (erga, plural) of the flesh are listed one by one in v.19: one crop from one source set against many deeds. Jesus uses the same word for trees and branches.

G2041.n: What a person does by effort. Paul pairs it with flesh in v.19, where fruit is what the Spirit produces.

G4151.n: One word for wind and spirit; Jesus plays on both meanings in John 3:8. It translates the Hebrew ruach in the Greek Old Testament.

H7307.n: Moves upon the waters in Gen 1:2; God puts his ruach within his people in Ezek 36:27. Context decides between wind, breath and spirit.

G26.n: Settled goodwill and self-giving. In John 21:15–17 Jesus asks twice with agapaō and the third time with phileō; Peter answers each time with phileō. The KJV renders both as love, and renders agapē as charity in 1 Cor 13.

G5368.n: Warm affection and friendship. Peter's word in all three of his answers in John 21:15–17.

G5479.n: Shares a root with charis (G5485), grace: joy as the response to a gift. Compare David's prayer for the joy (Hebrew sason) of salvation.

G1515.n: The Greek Old Testament uses it for shalom (H7965): wholeness and welfare, not only the absence of conflict.

G3115.n: Literally long-tempered: makros (long) + thumos (passion, anger). Thumos appears in the plural as wrath in v.20, so the list sets a slow temper against outbursts.

G5544.n: Kindness that is useful to others. The KJV says gentleness here and kindness elsewhere; the related verb is is kind in 1 Cor 13:4.

G19.n: Goodness in action, a word found only in Paul's letters. Built on agathos, the word for the good tree in Matt 7:17.

G4102.n: Both trust and trustworthiness. In a list of character qualities many translations read faithfulness; the KJV keeps faith.

G4236.n: Strength under control, not weakness. The adjective praus is Jesus' word in Matt 5:5 and 11:29, and the Greek Old Testament uses it of Moses in Num 12:3.

G1466.n: Literally power within: mastery of oneself. Paul reasoned with the governor Felix about it.

G4561.n: Can mean the body (the Word was made flesh) or human nature set against God (Gal 5:16–17). The same word carries both senses, so context decides.

G3056.n: A word as a whole message or reasoned account. Compare rhēma, a particular thing spoken. Jesus uses logos in John 15:3, the word which I have spoken.

G4487.n: A particular thing spoken. Hebrews says the worlds were framed by the rhēma of God, where John 1:1 calls the Word logos.

G746.n: John opens with Ἐν ἀρχῇ, the same words the Greek Old Testament uses to open Genesis.

G4637.n: From skēnē, tent, the Greek Old Testament word for the tabernacle. Dwelt among us is literally tabernacled among us.

G228.n: Genuine as opposed to copy or shadow; differs from alēthēs (G227), true as opposed to false. Jesus uses it for the true bread from heaven.

G2508.n: In v.2 the husbandman purgeth; in v.3 the disciples are already clean (katharoi), from the same root: the pruning image and the cleansing word are one idea.

G2513.n: Pure in heart uses the same word as clean in John 15:3.

G3306.n: Staying put in a relationship. Jesus uses it of the Spirit dwelling with the disciples and of branches abiding in the vine.

G3107.n: A state of being favoured, not a wish. The Greek Old Testament uses it for the Hebrew ashrei in Ps 1:1.

H835.n: A plural exclamation, roughly O the happiness of…, spoken over a way of life.

H7225.n: From rosh, head: the first, the starting point.

H1254.n: In the Old Testament this verb always has God as its subject. David uses it in Ps 51:10, create in me a clean heart.

H3820.n: The centre of thought, will and feeling, not only emotion.

H5342.n: A green shoot from a cut stump. Many readers hear it in Nazarene (Matt 2:23); Matthew does not quote Isaiah there, so treat it as a wordplay, not a citation.

H8451.n: Teaching and direction, wider than a legal code.

H2250.n: Peter echoes the line with the Greek mōlōps (G3468), bruise or welt.

G1632.n: Used of liquid poured out. Peter repeats the verb of the Greek Old Testament's Joel; the Hebrew is shaphak (H8210).

contrast: Set against each other in Galatians 5
